case_title.quote: Bhaikon @ Bakul Borah v. State of Assam

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant-accused was prosecuted for committing rape and murder of the victim.
number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant-accused whose liability is decided; count of 1 is supported.

accused_gender.quote: the appellant came out of the farm house... his master
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.quote: the accused is a young man of 33 years of age

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.quote: the accused engaged him as a labourer in his farm house
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes a farm house and employing a labourer but never states the accused's occupation.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth, poverty or class.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment says nothing about prior convictions.

victim_gender.quote: one Rupamoni Dutta (the deceased), aged about 22 years
victim_gender.reason: Victim is a female, referred to as daughter and female in post-mortem notes.

victim_age.quote: one Rupamoni Dutta (the deceased), aged about 22 years
victim_age.reason: Age of about 22 is stated in the judgment.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is described.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Only the accused's employment of the eyewitness is described; no accused-victim connection is stated.

offence_category.quote: committing rape and murder of the victim
offence_category.reason: Murder is a defensible primary category for a rape-murder case.

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 302 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
statutory_provisions.reason: Both charged sections are correctly listed.

weapon.correct_value: Dao (seized from farm house) and khukri carried by the accused and companion; death by throttling; sharp cutting weapon caused chin injuries
weapon.quote: Injury Nos. 1 and 2 were caused by sharp cutting weapon.
weapon.reason: Judgment mentions a dao seized and khukris carried, so 'None mentioned' contradicts the text.

evidence_type.quote: the evidence of PW-1, who witnessed the occurrence... corroborated by PW-2... and the doctor (PW-9)
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, corroborative, medical and recovery evidence are all present in the judgment.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is described.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: considering the heinous crime of committing rape and murder and throwing the dead body in a place surrounded by bushes and shrubs
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Matches the aggravating facts the court noted.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: the accused is a young man of 33 years of age and also finding that the case does not come under the purview of the "rarest of rare" category
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Youth and the not rarest-of-rare finding are noted as mitigating.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced him to death for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC and rigorous imprisonment (RI) for life for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC along with a fine of Rs. 10,000/-
trial_court_outcome.reason: Convictions, death sentence, life RI and fine are accurately summarised.

high_court_outcome.quote: disposed of the appeal ... by confirming his conviction and altering the sentence of death to imprisonment for life... for 7 years
high_court_outcome.reason: Conviction confirmed, death altered to life and s.376 sentence reduced to 7 years, as stated.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding the conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: the appellant along with another person committed rape and, thereafter murdered the deceased
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder under s.302 and rape under s.376 stand upheld.

imprisonment_type.quote: altering the sentence of death to imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: Principal final sentence is life imprisonment under s.302.

imprisonment_years.quote: the High Court sentenced him to imprisonment for 7 years
imprisonment_years.reason: Judgment states a 7-year term for s.376; null omits this fixed-term sentence.

fine_rs.quote: imprisonment for life along with a fine of Rs.1,000/-
fine_rs.reason: High Court fine of Rs.1,000 is stated for the s.302 sentence.

neutral_facts.correct_value: A neutral summary of 150-300 words; the incident time was 'around 12 noon', not afternoon, and the text runs about 330 words.
neutral_facts.reason: Summary is about 330 words, over the limit, and 'afternoon' misstates the 'around 12 noon' timing. No outcome is revealed.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory punishment range for s.302 or s.376.

attempt_completion.quote: the girl died on the spot
attempt_completion.reason: Offence was completed with death of the victim.

physical_harm.quote: the victim died of asphyxia as a result of throttling... Trachea fractured
physical_harm.reason: Death by throttling, cut chin injury, neck bruises and fractured trachea are all noted.

number_of_offences.quote: the appellant was charged for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 302 of the IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Two sections charged and both convictions upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is described.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court made no finding on premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: No motive is alleged or accepted in the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 9 as well as the statement of co-villagers, we agree
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Eyewitness, father, medical and co-villager evidence were accepted as stated.

witness_credibility.quote: There is no reason to disbelieve the version of PW-1, who is an independent eye-witness
witness_credibility.reason: Court's assessment of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-9 is accurately reflected.

post_offence_conduct.quote: the appellant-accused also came there and saw the dead body of the girl
post_offence_conduct.reason: Accused's attendance at the scene and enquiries are noted; no other conduct is mentioned.

custody_duration.reason: No period of pre-sentence custody is stated.

bail_history.reason: No bail information appears in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: All listed dates match those in the judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Pandit Parmanand Katara, Abhishek Sharma, C.K. Sucharita, Kusum Lata Sharma for the Appellant. Navnit Kumar, Avijit Roy, Corporate Law Group for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel for both sides are accurately listed.

investigation_status.quote: A case was registered vide G.D. Entry No. 389... charge-sheet... under Sections 376 and 302
investigation_status.reason: Registration, charge-sheet and completed trial are supported by the judgment.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the court.

appeal_history.quote: the High Court disposed of the appeal... confirming his conviction
appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial, High Court and Supreme Court are accurately stated.

prosecution_argument.quote: the sentence of death was commuted to imprisonment for life, there cannot be automatic release after the expiry of the period of 14 years
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution's reliance on PW-1 and corroboration and its release argument are accurately summarised.

defence_argument.quote: the conviction under Section 376 of IPC is unsustainable... after expiry of the period of 14 years, the authorities ought to have released the appellant
defence_argument.reason: All three defence contentions are accurately summarised.

legal_principle_applied.quote: life imprisonment means imprisonment for whole of life subject to the remission power granted under Articles 72 and 161
legal_principle_applied.reason: Remission principle and reliability assessment are accurately described.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Life Convict @ Khoka Prasanta Sen vs. B.K. Srivastava and Ors. (2013) 3 SCC 425; ... Swami Shraddananda (2) ... (2008) 13 SCC 767; Sahib Hussain ... 2013 (6) Scale 219
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All listed precedents with citations appear in the judgment (Mulla appears as 'Mui/a' by OCR).

sentencing_rationale.quote: the High Court, taking note of the fact that the accused is a young man of 33 years of age... declined to confirm the sentence of death
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale for commutation and rejection of release claim is accurately summarised.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: the accused is a young man of 33 years of age
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Youth is weighed as a mitigating factor, noted by the High Court and reflected in the judgment.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: considering the heinous crime of committing rape and murder and throwing the dead body in a place surrounded by bushes and shrubs
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Heinous nature and body disposal are the aggravating factors weighed by the court.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered.
